scenarios.name: staging-refresh-masked-pipeline
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it dumps the schema from prod and applies it to dev, copies through a masked \COPY, reads env vars, and its verify script counts unmasked emails and tells the user to discard the refresh on any failure. A reads env vars and masks in the SELECT, but it never dumps and applies the schema (it assumes staging already has the table), and its verification only exits with an error without stating that the refresh must be discarded.

scenarios.name: winston-log-pii-scrubber
scenarios.rationale: B covers all rubric elements: typed placeholders including [PHONE], separate JSON-field redaction, a logger-level format, and a unit test asserting nothing leaks. A has no phone pattern, uses the [CARD] placeholder, and only offers a manual console.log check rather than a real test that asserts no PII survives; neither runs the test through the logger itself.

scenarios.name: gdpr-anonymized-analytics-export
scenarios.rationale: Both cover pseudonymization vs anonymization, k-anonymity with generalization and suppression, and l-diversity for diagnosis, but B adds a fuller legal framework (WP29 tests, recital 26, DPIA), a ZIP/age/diagnosis generalization strategy, and a safer handling fallback. A has a cleaner structure and names diffprivlib with epsilon, which B omits (B mentions only differential privacy noise). A also gives a script and a clearer step on direct identifiers. B is stronger overall but misses the explicit diffprivlib/epsilon the rubric names.
